name: Nuss
prior: Bouncing-object exciters and sequencers exist: Ableton/AAS Tension offers 'bow, hammer, bouncing hammer and plectrum' as exciters (VS: researchcatalogue.net/view/1579904/1589043 on Collision/Corpus/Tension); SuperCollider TBall UGen 'models the impacts of a bouncing object that is reflected by a vibrating surface' with gravity and damping (VS: help.sccode.org/UGens/Generators/PhysicalModels/TBall.html); Andy Farnell's 'bouncing ball' in Designing Sound and its Csound port (VS: csound.com/icsc2022/proceedings Implementing Andy Farnell's bouncing ball); Cycles and Spots TableBounce VST3 - a physics engine triggers notes from two wavetable synths, gravity and ball speed adjustable (VS: kvraudio.com/product/tablebounce-by-cycles-and-spots); BounceBud iOS/macOS MIDI balls (VS: synthanatomy.com/2023/09/bouncebud...); Sinevibes Dispersion v2 'bouncing ball delay' (VS: sinevibes.com/dispersion); RhythmicBall browser studio (VS: rhythmicball.com); LDM Gravity Pack M4L (VS: isotonikstudios.com/product/gravity-pack); Synplant 'Jingle Balls' easter egg (VS: forum.renoise.com ... bouncing-ball-effect). Not confirmed: a bounce exciter in Chromaphone 3 or Reason Objekt (search found none). Rare: bounce as an exciter is textbook (Farnell, SC) and shipped (Tension); a pitched touch source with finger height = drop height, Hertz-contact cascades and a Puls that catches the cascade was not found - but the mechanism is well known and the idea itself rates the novelty as 'mittel'.
costNotes: Native, same path as Saite: offline render in the existing DSP worker (dspJob + KS_CACHE LRU 80 / 1e7 frames, nearest cached buffer retuned by playbackRate, verified APP: index.html 4648-4681, VCOST1.sai = 0.35 at 2081) then BufferSource + lowpass + optional body peaking -> 0.35-0.4 at level 1; level 3 stereo pair ~0.6. Render measured (M: sim/eng_min5.js, Node x64): 2.9-3.4 ms for a 1.4-s buffer with 4 board modes + 2 nut modes + roll noise; phone x2-3 in the worker -> 6-10 ms off-thread, fine; first-touch miss falls back to the nearest cached key, as Saite does. Cache: 6 y-steps x 3 sizes x 2 variants per semitone = 36 keys per semitone, so the LRU 80 holds ~2 semitones of full variety - the +-2-semitone retune covers that, bounce intervals then scale by +-12 % (inaudible as physics, audible as rhythm only on the Puls grid). Warm only the current y-step +-1 and the current scale, like warmKS.
soundHeld: The physics as specified is at the wrong scale: h0 = 0.05-0.65 m and e = 0.45-0.85 give a first flight 2 v0 / g = 0.20-0.73 s and a total cascade 2 v0 / g / (1 - e) = 0.36 s (y = 0) to 4.9 s (y = 1) - the upper half of Hoehe is a slow 'tock ... tock .. tock' loop, not a hit, and the buffers are 2-5 s long (cache pressure). Dropping from finger height instead (h0 = 0.5-6 cm, v0 = 0.3-1.1 m/s) gives 4 bounces in 0.10 s (y 0.2), 7 in 0.21 s (y 0.5), 15 in 0.52 s (y 0.9) (M: sim with the equivalent time factor) - that is the musical scale; keep the Hertz laws (tau ~ v^-1/5, amp ~ v^6/5) which make each hit a diminishing accelerando. Held is struck: after the roll (<= 300 ms) there is silence, setY cannot change the cascade in flight (buffer is fixed), setF only via playbackRate - acceptable inside Myzel's struck family (Saite, Tropfen) but no held expression at all, and Gestik Hoehe offsets only affect the next hit. Identity risk: the board is a free-free bar (1 : 2.572 : 4.644), i.e. the Kalimba/marimba family already in the library, so a single bounce sounds like Kalimba; the cascade is the only difference, and the geometric e-series is so recognisable that after three hits the listener hears 'the bouncing-ball sample' (Farnell's demo), not a nut. Mitigation: vary e per bounce +-10 % (grain irregularity), random nut spin (second nut mode detune), 3 sizes by vel, and the roll noise as the tail.
soundBurst: As a Puls hit it is a built-in fill: one trigger = 4-15 accelerating taps, so a sparse lane (1/4 or 1/2 step) yields accelerando figures no other engine has. Two problems: (1) bounce times are geometric, never on the grid - with cascades longer than one step and 2-4 lanes it is rhythmic mush, so the default cascade must be shorter than the lane's step (y low, or gate-cut); (2) 'gefangen' via decayMul -> e means a new render per e value (key explosion) - cut with the native envelope at gate end instead ('in die Hand gefangen', muffled lowpass + fast release) and let decayMul choose among 3 e-steps only. Sporenregen/Rassel triggering Nuss cascades works for free.
failureModes: Drop heights of 5-65 cm give 0.2-0.7 s first gaps and up to 5-s cascades - must be scaled to finger height (0.5-6 cm) or a time factor; buffers otherwise 2-5 s
Reads as 'the bouncing-ball sample' after a few hits; needs per-bounce e variation and spin, not just +-3 % jitter
Free-free bar body = Kalimba cousin; a single bounce is indistinguishable from Kalimba
No held expression: y and Hoehe offsets act only on the next hit; setF by playbackRate shifts the bounce rhythm +-12 % within the retune window
Puls: geometric times vs grid - cascades longer than a step make mush across lanes; decayMul-driven e explodes the cache
Cache: 36 keys per semitone, LRU 80 - only ~2 semitones of full variety resident; cold keys play retuned neighbours with shifted bounce timing
'Niedlich' image; the serious deep presets the idea proposes depend on the roll-noise tail and low board tuning
verdict: Rare at best: bounce exciters are textbook (Farnell, SuperCollider TBall) and shipped (Ableton Tension's bouncing hammer, TableBounce, BounceBud, Dispersion); the touch framing with finger height as drop height is new, the sound is not. Native and cheap (Saite's path, 0.35-0.4 units, render measured ~3 ms per buffer), but the physics is specified at the wrong scale - 5-65 cm drops give half-second gaps and 5-s cascades; nut-from-finger-height (0.5-6 cm) gives the 4-15 bounces in 0.1-0.5 s that read as a hit. The body is a free-free bar like Kalimba, so one bounce is Kalimba and three are 'the bouncing-ball sample'. Keep it only as the showcase of the offline path with per-bounce variation and the gate-cut 'gefangen' Puls gesture; otherwise fold it into Kalimba/Saite as an exciter option ('Prallen') and save the library slot for an engine with held expression.
